paragraphs: In the morning, assess new clients, administer scales, and schedule counseling plans. At midday, conduct several individual sessions and use cognitive behavioral techniques to break down problems. In the afternoon, lead a group or make a home visit and engage family members. Before leaving, update records and follow-ups and prepare crisis response plans.

In short, they help people trapped in difficult circumstances return to a healthier path. Their work includes assessment, counseling, planning, coordination, follow-up, and crisis intervention. It requires both thought and empathy and forms the front line of psychological recovery.
